# mpadge.eu

> Personal site of Mark Padgham: open-source software developer (C++, R, JavaScript, Rust), reformed academic, developer of the UrbanAnalyst platform, and former lead of software peer-review for rOpenSci. The blog covers programming in R and C++, open-source software communities, and the effects of AI on code and society.

All software is open-source. Code is hosted on GitHub, Codeberg, Codefloe, SourceHut and tangled (all as `mpadge`). Mastodon: https://nerdculture.de/@mpadge

## Main pages

- [About](https://mpadge.eu/about/): Background, availability for hire, and about this site
- [Blog](https://mpadge.eu/blog/): All blog posts
- [Code](https://mpadge.eu/code/): Software packages developed
- [Privacy](https://mpadge.eu/privacy/): Privacy policy
- [RSS feed](https://mpadge.eu/feed.xml): Blog feed

## Blog posts

- [Distributed Git](https://mpadge.eu/blog/git-push.html): How to redefine git push for an era of distributed code.
- [Coding Alone](https://mpadge.eu/blog/coding-alone.html): In which I show how, over the last few years, the world has rapidly moved from open-source software being produced and maintained by online communities, to software projects being built and maintained in isolation.
- [Machina machista](https://mpadge.eu/blog/machina-machista.html): Your AI thinks you're a dude.
- [Purposeful joy](https://mpadge.eu/blog/purposeful-joy.html): The current purpose for a select few is to help computer programs replace the purposeful labour of a generation of uniquely idiosyncratic human beings.
- [Our goodpractice Package Has New Superpowers](https://mpadge.eu/blog/goodpractice.html): We have worked hard over the past few months on major upgrades to our goodpractice package.
- [Centralisation, reversibility, and restarting](https://mpadge.eu/blog/centralisation-reversibility.html): Technical progress tends toward centralisation: telephone multiplexing made calls easier and centralised the entire telephone industry; GitHub made coding easier and centralised the world of software development.
- [Debugging C++ code in R with a single command](https://mpadge.eu/blog/r-cpp-debugging.html): There are several great references for how to debug C or C++ code in R, but descriptions of how to start a debugger are often not so informative.
- [Timeout on parallel jobs in R](https://mpadge.eu/blog/r-parallel-timeout.html): Python's multiprocessing and threading libraries both have a timeout parameter for re-joining threads after they've finished.
- [GitHub notifications from the terminal](https://mpadge.eu/blog/github-terminal-notifications.html): I work almost entirely from the terminal, and regret the few remaining tasks which still require me to venture elsewhere, such as a web browser.
- [The allcontributors package](https://mpadge.eu/blog/allcontributors.html): An alternative implementation in R of the original 'allcontributors.org' to acknowledge all contributors in your 'README' (or elsewhere).
- [The troubles with getting help files in R](https://mpadge.eu/blog/r-help-files.html): A primer on ways to extract the actual content of help files.
- [Using RcppParallel to aggregate to a vector](https://mpadge.eu/blog/rcppparallel-aggregation.html): This article was recently published in the Rcpp Gallery, and demonstrates using the RcppParallel package to aggregate to an output vector.
- [Github 2FA, git push, and password entry](https://mpadge.eu/blog/github-2fa-push.html): Activating github two-factor authentication (2FA) offers an indubitable security boost, with one notable side effect--https authentication requires entering a Personal Access Token instead of password.
- [What are matrices in R?](https://mpadge.eu/blog/r-matrices.html): If everything in R is a vector, then what is a matrix?
- [Calling external files from C in R](https://mpadge.eu/blog/c-external-files.html): I recently encountered a problem while bundling an old C library into a new R package.
- [Caching via background R processes](https://mpadge.eu/blog/background-process-caching.html): Caching is implemented because it saves time, generally by saving the results of one function call for subsequent reuse.
- [C++ templates and Rcpp](https://mpadge.eu/blog/rcpp-cpp-templates.html): C++ templates are really useful.
- [how i made this site](https://mpadge.eu/blog/making-this-site.html): This site is built with zurb foundation, because i had read that it did everything that hugo could, but that final products were more lightweight and flexible.
